sections.title: Submit Proposed Protocols Online
sections.content:
Jon Postel asks that proposed protocols be submitted as online documents, preferably as NLS files at the Network Information Center. He says online documents make review easier, allow editorial and substantive changes to proceed quickly, support timely updates, and are easy to distribute to the network community.

He asks anyone who has great difficulty complying to contact him.
sections.plainLanguage: Protocol proposals should be shared as online files. This makes them easier to review, change, update and distribute.

sections.title: Telnet Subnegotiation Ending
sections.content:
The note says all existing Telnet options that use subnegotiation are modified as described in RFC 562. A subnegotiation string ends with IAC SE, where the value of SE is 240.

If a subnegotiation contains a byte with value 255 (IAC), the sender must transmit that byte twice.
sections.plainLanguage: A Telnet subnegotiation ends with the two-byte marker IAC SE. If the data itself contains IAC, send that byte twice.

sections.title: Updated Contact Information
sections.content: The note gives Jon Postel's new mailing address at The MITRE Corporation in McLean, Virginia. Online messages can be addressed to POSTEL@ISI or to JBP in the NIC Journal.
sections.plainLanguage: The note also gives a new mailing address and two ways to send the author an online message.

references.text: RFC 562, cited for the Telnet subnegotiation modification.
